title: Web font basics and responsible loading
learningObjectives: Explain web font basics and responsible loading and apply it in a readable interface.

understand.concept: Web fonts let a page load font files rather than relying only on installed system fonts. @font-face defines a family and its source. Use appropriate formats, provide fallbacks, and consider font-display so text remains visible while a font loads.
understand.whyItMatters: Font files affect performance, privacy, licensing, and layout. Load only needed weights and subsets, use trustworthy sources, and test glyph coverage for all target languages.
understand.analogy: A web font is an optional resource delivered with the page. The page should remain readable if that resource is delayed or unavailable.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy builds intuition; actual rendering follows CSS layout rules and browser specifications.

explain.narrative: This safe demonstration uses a locally available font source. A production rule would point to a properly licensed font file.

examples.code: Readable text with a fallback stack.
examples.explanation: This safe demonstration uses a locally available font source. A production rule would point to a properly licensed font file.
examples.expectedOutput: A browser-rendered demonstration of the CSS behaviour described in this lesson.

practise.guidedTask: Define a local or licensed font with @font-face and a generic fallback. Explain what happens if the font cannot load.
